title: Wynter
sceneText:
When you got up this morning the wind had changed.

Martha was pickling the last batch first thing, saying that with this weather it would be too late if she did not. Gregor fed the horses early, two hours before he usually does. Nobody said why. They simply did it.

By dusk it had dropped far enough to see your breath.

There is somebody standing outside the main gate.

One man, in a dark coat, no hat. He is standing at the end of Maplegate Avenue looking at the two rows of trees. Most of the leaves are down; what is left is all dark brown.

He hears you come out and turns round.

“Forgive me,” he says. “I came down from the north, saw this road, and stood longer than I meant to.”

He introduces himself. A scholar, passing through, working on something in the way of local records. He gives a name.

Wynter.

You ask him in for something hot. He says there is no need; he has to press on, and must be at Valehold before dark.

But he does not go.

variants.tier1:
You stand at the gate and exchange a few words.

He asks about the harvest hereabouts, and when the two rows of maples along Maplegate Avenue were planted. You do not know. You say you have only been here a month.

“A month,” he says. “Then you caught the best of it.”

He looks up at the sky.

“It turns cold from today. Once the wind goes round like this, frost comes after.”

“How do you know?”

“I came from the north,” he says. “There has already been one up there.”

He thanks you and goes off in the direction of Valehold.

You stand at the gate a while before going in. It has gone fully dark.
variants.tier2_open:
He asks several questions. He asks them too specifically.

You answer some of them. You do not know yourself why you would say any of this to a stranger. Probably because he knows nobody here, and because everything you have said this month has been remembered by somebody.

When you have finished he thinks about it a while.

“These things you have told me,” he says. “The order seems wrong.”

“Meaning?”

“You gave them in the order you came to know them,” he says. “That is not the order they happened in.”
variants.tier2_close:
Having said that, he stops.

“There are pieces missing,” he says. “Pieces missing in the middle, so there is no telling whether they are one thing or several.”

He turns up the collar of his coat.

“I cannot fill them in for you. I know nothing about any of it. All I have done is put what you said into another order.”

He takes two steps towards the avenue and stops again.

“The missing pieces should all be in the hands of people you know.”
variants.tier3:
He asks several questions. He asks them too specifically.

You answer. You say more than you had meant to.

When you have finished he does not speak at once. He stands there looking at the end of the avenue, as though waiting for something to settle into place.

“Let me say it back in order,” he says. “Tell me whether it is right.”

“Some of it you told me, and some of it I am inferring.” He says this part first. “I shall be clear about which is inference.”

“This man had been here a long time. His father did the same work — that part is yours. So he never chose it. He took it on.”

“In some year he began checking things it was not his place to check. He went on checking for several years.”

“He found something, and the something is not a crime. That part is inference, because if it were a crime it would have been settled long ago. Only a thing that is not a crime drags on that long.”

“He went and asked people. Church, nobility, government.” He counts them off. “Three at the least. Nobody gave him an answer.”

“This part is inference too: the way he asked was not asking for help. He wrapped it up as a technical question. So nobody heard that he was asking for help.”

“The years after that, he was stepping back. Back behind other people, where he could not be found.”

“This summer he stopped answering any request at all.” He pauses. “You said it was as though he could not hear. I think he heard. There was simply nowhere left in him to put it.”

“The night before he went, he burned things. Things written over many times. Written many times means he had been wanting to say it. Burned means that at the end he decided not to.”

“The next morning he rode away. The room was left tidier than usual.”

He has finished.

“The tidiness is the important part,” he adds. “A man leaving in a hurry does not tidy the room.”

The wind pushes a layer of fallen leaves along the avenue.

“All of that is what you already knew,” he says. “I have added nothing.”

“Then how can you set it out like that?”

He thinks about it.

“Because I do not know them,” he says.

“Every person you know holds one piece, and every piece is stuck to the person holding it. Stuck to their position, to how far they can go, to who they owe and who owes them.”

“Those things are useful to you, because you have to go on living here.”

“They are no use to me. I leave tomorrow.”

He draws his hands into his sleeves.

“So I can lay them side by side. That is not a skill. That is the advantage of somebody passing through.”
variants.tier4:
He has already turned to go, and after a few steps he stops.

“One more thing.”

He looks back.

“What you said just now. Which direction the horse came back from. Which side the shoe was worn on. What kind of mud was on its legs. Where the thing in its mane grows.”

“You gave me those four things very clearly.”

“You know where he is.”

You say nothing.

“I am not asking you,” he says. “I am telling you that you already know.”

He looks at the light.

“You may have been waiting for somebody to come and tell you what to do.”

“There is no such person. What you have is enough. Give it to somebody who can use it.”

This time he really goes.

Halfway down the avenue he raises a hand without looking back.

That night brought the first hard frost of the autumn.
variants.tier2_count: “These things you have told me. Let me count them.”
variants.shape_motive: “Several of them are about time. After a certain year, this man was not what he had been.”
variants.shape_officer: “One of them is about quantities. What somebody declared and what somebody did do not agree, and the amount they do not agree by is too small — small enough that nobody would act on it.”
variants.shape_noble: “One of them is about a visit. He went to somebody he should not have gone to. I mean that the person could not answer what he wanted to ask.”
variants.shape_position: “And one of them is about a horse.”
variants.tier2_cannot:
He stops.

“These may be one thing, and they may be three.”

“What you have given me is not enough for me to judge.”
